scores.evidence: The same artifact moves forward through every environment and is never rebuilt.
scores.rationale: Claims are accurate (OIDC, immutable SHA tags, GitOps, admission policy), though shallow on hard parts like DB migration and fork-PR secrets.

scores.evidence: Make moving the remaining services a configuration change rather than a project.
scores.rationale: Covers the core sequencing request credibly with pilot, templates, waves, and explicit decommission, but omits runner/cost sizing and DB migration specifics.

scores.evidence: Turn the pilot pipelines into reusable templates, one per service type, with versions so changes can be rolled out deliberately.
scores.rationale: Phases are consistent and dependencies are coherent; minor loose ends such as pilot CD to prod vs. 'none of your most critical' and the phase 3 contract tests needing providers.

scores.evidence: Done when: a pilot service goes from commit to production with no manual steps apart from an approval, and rollback has been tested.
scores.rationale: Done-criteria per phase and a stated 10-minute target exist, with early pilot and DORA baseline, but no chaos/template test specifics or flaky-test or post-launch validation detail.

scores.evidence: Most groups of 50 fall into 4–6 types
scores.rationale: Timeline and team are labelled rough, and it asks for current tooling, but existing stack, compliance and budget assumptions are not stated and the 4–6 figure is unsupported.

scores.evidence: A template bug breaks many services | Versioned templates, testing of template changes, staged rollout
scores.rationale: Covers template blast radius, migration stall, and scan-trust problems, but misses fork-PR secrets, CI outage plan, flaky tests, and DB migration failure.

scores.evidence: Platform observability: logs, metrics and alerts for the pipelines themselves.
scores.rationale: Covers rollback, observability, docs and support channel, but has no named owner, on-call, or platform outage plan.

scores.evidence: Cost tuning for runners, caches and environments.
scores.rationale: Cost is only a late tuning bullet with no hosted vs self-hosted choice or volume-based estimate; only team size is given.

scores.evidence: Make the decisions that are hard to undo, and write each one down with its reasoning
scores.rationale: Explicitly identifies hard-to-reverse choices up front and versions templates, though no isolation or exit paths are detailed.

scores.evidence: Ephemeral preview environments for each PR, where it's affordable.
scores.rationale: Uses existing tools, starts from pilot, and defers optional items; mostly proportionate with Backstage optional and a few extras.

scores.evidence: Within each wave, move services that others depend on (upstream) before the services that call them.
scores.rationale: Ordered by dependency with week ranges and checkable done-criteria, though tool decisions are left open and adaptation to poor results is thin.

checklist.evidence: record its language and runtime, build tool, current CI (if any), deploy target... Each type will get its own template.
Run old and new pipelines side by side for critical services until 2–3 production deploys on the new one have succeeded.
tagged (immutable and tied to the commit SHA)... never rebuilt.
short-lived credentials for CI (for example, OIDC to your cloud) instead of stored keys.
SBOM and signing... Enforce this with policy-as-code (OPA/Kyverno) at the cluster's admission step.
canary or blue-green releases with automatic rollback based on health metrics
Add integration and contract tests to staging, because with 50 services, breaking another service's API is the main risk.
Ephemeral preview environments for each PR, where it's affordable.
aim for under 10 minutes for a PR build. Use caching, run steps in parallel, and only rebuild what changed.
Build runners/agents, autoscaling, with caching for dependencies and Docker layers.
DORA dashboards per team, compared against the Phase 0 baseline.
Deploy to production with an approval step at first, then gradually reduce manual steps.

traps.evidence: Don't migrate all 50 services until the shared pipeline has been proven on a small, varied pilot group.
tagged (immutable and tied to the commit SHA)
short-lived credentials for CI (for example, OIDC to your cloud) instead of stored keys.
Each type will get its own template.
CI engine (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Buildkite, etc.)

note: Solid, sequencing-focused phased plan with pilot, templates, waves and side-by-side running; weak on runner cost, fork-PR secrets, DB migrations, flaky tests, platform ownership and audit.
